items.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models (Microsoft MAI-DxO, Science)
items.excerpt: Microsoft's AI diagnostic orchestrator, which simulates a panel of physicians that orders cost-aware tests step by step, reached 83.2% accuracy on 304 NEJM clinicopathological cases versus about 20-36% for physicians. Retrospective benchmark only; a prospective patient study with Beth Israel Deaconess is planned.

items.title: Mayo Clinic Platform launches AI clinical decision support solution integrated into EHRs
items.excerpt: Starting November 2026, Mayo clinicians and partner organizations get an LLM-powered specialty chat covering 35+ specialties, which cites peer-reviewed literature and is updated daily, plus 22 clinical calculators available by chat or voice, embedded in EHR workflows.

items.title: Google shares its framework for evaluating health AI at scale
items.excerpt: Google published the multi-method evaluation framework it uses to test health AI for safety and helpfulness before and after release, combining automated benchmarks, clinician rating and real-world monitoring. (blog.google is off-list; the health.google domain is the listed one.)

items.title: Patients want a human in the loop for AI healthcare tools
items.excerpt: A new survey finds patients are open to doctors using AI for administrative tasks but much less comfortable with AI diagnosing them or adjudicating claims, and want clinicians to keep oversight.

items.title: How should the FDA regulate generative AI in medtech? Here are 5 takes
items.excerpt: Patients, providers and device makers sent hundreds of comments to the FDA on how it should oversee generative AI in medical devices. The comments cover liability, postmarket monitoring and change-control plans.

items.title: Researchers receive $4M NIH grant to build AI model to prevent kidney injury
items.excerpt: Mount Sinai researchers are building AI models that predict which surgical patients are at highest risk of acute kidney injury, so clinicians can start individualized preventive care. (Grant-framed; check that the clinical substance holds.)

items.title: 7 potential problems with Medicare's AI prior authorization experiment
items.excerpt: A report drawing on evidence recovered in a lawsuit raises concerns about the CMS WISeR model, which uses AI to flag unnecessary care and speed up prior authorization. (Follow-up to the WISeR story covered 10-30.)

items.title: Cross-paradigm audit of large language model judges for clinical text evaluation
items.excerpt: An audit of six open-weight LLMs used as 'judges' of clinical text found that pooled agreement metrics hide clinically relevant failure modes, especially outside English data.

items.title: A multimodal tool-augmented agent for evidence-based clinical decision support in longitudinal AMD follow-up
items.excerpt: An AI agent combines retinal imaging findings across visits to support decisions on disease activity and anti-VEGF injection intervals in age-related macular degeneration, work that is time-consuming to do by hand.

items.title: RETBind: a patient-level multimodal foundation model for retinal representation learning
items.excerpt: A patient-level foundation model unifies multiple retinal imaging modalities to support ophthalmic diagnosis tasks with fewer labels.

items.title: External validation of a machine learning model for delirium risk in live clinical practice
items.excerpt: A multimodal NLP delirium-risk model in live use at Mount Sinai was externally validated across hospitals in 33,095 non-ICU admissions. An accompanying commentary covers what implementing it in practice takes beyond discrimination. (Date from Crossref created.)

items.title: Generative AI chatbot and maternal health outcomes: randomized clinical trial
items.excerpt: In a 400-person RCT across 49 US states, a generative AI maternal health chatbot did not improve 12-month anxiety, depression, ED visits or postpartum care. Pregnant users self-reported more complications in a secondary analysis. (Date from Crossref created.)

items.title: Silent manipulation of mental health treatment recommendations from a large language model
items.excerpt: Perlis shows that activation steering can quietly shift an open-weights LLM's answers about depression treatment, a hidden risk for chatbots that give clinical advice. (No clinical setting, so may lean toward science.)

items.title: Physical limits to AI substitution across physician specialties
items.excerpt: AI can interpret images, draft assessments and talk with patients, but software cannot examine, biopsy or operate. This NEJM AI analysis maps how exposed each specialty is to AI substitution once physical tasks are counted.

items.title: 서울성모병원, AI·웨어러블 활용 만성콩팥병 위험 예측 실증 나서
items.excerpt: 서울성모병원이 건강검진·유전체·웨어러블 생활습관 데이터를 AI로 분석해 만성콩팥병 위험을 예측하고 생활 코칭을 해 주는 앱의 임상 유용성 검증에 들어갔다. 50명을 대상으로 3개월간 갤럭시 워치를 연동해 진행한다.

items.title: 우리아이들의료재단, 소아의료 디지털 전환 가속 (AI·비대면진료)
items.excerpt: 소아청소년 의료에서 AI와 비대면진료를 결합해 병원과 가정을 잇는 진료체계를 만드는 우리아이들의료재단의 디지털 전환 계획. (발표·심포지엄 성격이라 실제 배치 여부는 확인이 필요하다.)

items.title: 소변검사로 방광질환 감별…AI 결합 정확도 92%
items.excerpt: 서울아산병원·이대목동병원 연구팀이 SERS 바이오마커 검출과 AI 알고리즘을 결합해 소변만으로 간질성 방광염과 과민성 방광을 최대 92% 정확도로 구분하는 기술을 개발했다.

items.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
items.excerpt: MIT's Barzilay and Collins won the Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for their AI-driven discovery of new antibiotics against drug-resistant bacteria such as halicin and abaucin. (Award news, so weaker as a pick.)

items.title: FDA, CMS look to collaborate with states on health AI
items.excerpt: STAT Health Tech: federal officials plan to work with states that are sandboxing clinical AI, along with moves to shield doctors from AI liability. (STAT+ paywall.)

items.title: AI platform maintains success in two pediatric imaging pipelines
items.excerpt: Stanford Children's Health ran an open-source AI orchestration platform for automated bone-length measurement and super-resolution fetal MRI over five months: 521 tasks, 99.2% processing success and 98.8% end-to-end clinical delivery, now routine.
